Holding the processor awake so a turn survives the screen going off. Stop the harness from its menu to release it.
Workspace saved for the next harness start. Existing sessions retain their recorded location.
Move the project to shared storage?

DSH can keep its projects in /sdcard/DSH instead of a folder private to the app. Files there open in other applications, appear in your file manager, and survive reinstalling the app. New sessions use the new location.
Moving the project to shared storage…
Grant all-files access first; without it nothing can be written to shared storage.
Stop the harness before changing the workspace. Existing sessions keep their recorded project location.

This stops the harness and any active turn, then copies and verifies your projects. Original files stay in place. Conflicts or failures keep the current workspace unchanged. Start the harness again after the copy.
Copied %1$d; verified identical: %2$d. Workspace: %3$s. Original files are retained. Start the harness to use this location; earlier sessions keep their recorded project location.
The workspace was not changed. Original files are retained. Resolve the following problems and retry: %1$s
A project copy is already running.

Default: confirm tools that can change files or run code. Read and search tools continue directly. Changes apply after stopping and starting the harness, including resumed sessions. This adds approval; Android commands still have no project sandbox.

Autonomous mode allows tools without this additional confirmation. Commands and code can access DSH’s private files, including credentials, and any shared files allowed by Android. A working directory does not confine commands. Enable only for projects and instructions you trust.
Execution preference saved. Stop and start the harness to apply it.
